name: Private fund advisers

subjectOf.text: Registering large private fund advisers works by increasing the volume of data available to regulators, which in turn may help protect against systemic risk.
subjectOf.abstract: The registration of large private fund advisers increases the availability of data and may help protect against systemic risk.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Investment Adviser Regulation (2013). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2337268
scope_conditions: large private fund advisers registered with the SEC

subjectOf.text: Further randomization of the sample was not available as a remedy, because respondents drawn from outside the private fund adviser population would never have been exposed to the new disclosure requirements and so could say nothing about them.
subjectOf.abstract: It would not have been feasible to further randomize the sample by including respondents from outside of the private fund industry or respondents other than private fund advisers because those non-adviser respondents would not have been exposed to the new disclosure requirements.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Private Fund Disclosures Under the Dodd-Frank Act (2014). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2447306
scope_conditions: surveys measuring the experience of complying with a new disclosure regime

subjectOf.text: Despite contacting the entire population of 3669 SEC-registered private fund advisers by fax and e-mail over more than five months, the study obtained only 52 respondents, a response rate of 0.014 percent.
subjectOf.abstract: After multiple attempts to reach the entire population in over five months, respondents ([n=52]) (0.014%) answered questions in several categories designed to identify the effectiveness of Form PF.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Private Fund Disclosures Under the Dodd-Frank Act (2014). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2447306
scope_conditions: survey fielded after the first mandatory Form PF filing deadline

subjectOf.text: Advisers themselves understand Form PF's purpose the way the statute frames it: most respondents identified assessing systemic risk and closing the historical information gap about private funds as the form's purpose.
subjectOf.abstract: Most advisers assert that the purpose of Form PF is to assess systemic risk and address the lack of information regarding private funds.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Private Fund Disclosures Under the Dodd-Frank Act (2014). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2447306

subjectOf.text: Contrary to the industry's public complaints about SEC support, a majority of respondents rated the best level of SEC staff guidance available for completing Form PF as sufficient or good.
subjectOf.abstract: A majority of respondents assessed the best level of SEC guidance in the context of their Form PF completion as sufficient or good.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Private Fund Disclosures Under the Dodd-Frank Act (2014). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2447306

subjectOf.text: The survey achieved a response rate of 5.44 percent from a population of 1267 registered private fund advisers.
subjectOf.abstract: The response rate for this survey was 5.44% of a population of 1267.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, The Private Fund Industry Five Years after the Dodd-Frank Act – A Survey Study (2016). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2732915
scope_conditions: e-mail survey of advisers registered before the March 30, 2012 effective date

subjectOf.text: Because private fund advisers prefer confidentiality and generally oppose publicity, most do not respond to survey questions, which makes obtaining a substantial effective sample size for survey studies of this industry difficult.
subjectOf.abstract: Most private fund advisers do not respond to survey questions so obtaining a substantial effective sample size for survey studies with private fund advisers is difficult.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, The Private Fund Industry Five Years after the Dodd-Frank Act – A Survey Study (2016). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2732915
scope_conditions: survey research targeting private fund advisers
